A subscriber asked me: What do I read daily & who do I follow?

I will start with a few principles
1. A good writer isn't someone elaborate, or sophisticated. It's someone who can explain concepts simply, and someone you simply enjoy reading

2. It is far more important to choose what NOT to read, than what to read. You curate your diet. You don't eat junk foods. You don't consume too much sugar. Likewise, your mental diet has to be curated. You don't consume tabloids. You don't consume Tiktok slop 

3. Gell-Mann Amnesia: A cognitive bias where a person spots major errors in a news story about a topic they know well, but then reads the rest of the newspaper and trusts everything else as if it were completely accurate.

Hence, always read people who write about topics you know they're knowledgeable in

4. Lastly, consume broadly. I actually don't like reading Financial News that much, because it's my work. Instead, I get more value reading *non-financial* stuff.

1. @kylascan for Economics 
2. @PaulSkallas for esoteric wisdom
3. @robkhenderson for Sociology
4. @FT for financial-related news 
5. MicroCapClub & @howardmarks for investing
6. Fiction Books - Dune, LOTR, Enders Game, etc. Fiction books are really great for cognitive breaks
